_comment: Bundled synthetic example for /graph/. Entity and predicate texts are verbatim from Artifact #12 (Appendix A, Canonical Entity Registry: Definition; Appendix C, Canonical Relationship Registry: Meaning and Constraint). scripts/check-graph.mjs fails the build if any text, type or predicate drifts from docs/12-ontology-specification.md. Names, labels, conditions and positions are invented for illustration.

Actor.definition: A human, organizational or machine-associated entity capable of initiating, approving, influencing or being accountable for activity.

HumanIdentity.definition: An identity representing a human actor.

Agent.definition: A software entity that selects, sequences or executes steps toward an objective using models, tools, memory, rules or other agents.

Tool.definition: A callable capability through which a model, agent, application or workflow can observe, retrieve, transform or change external state.

BusinessAction.definition: An action that creates a business, operational, customer, financial, legal or organizational effect.

Outcome.definition: An observed or intended result of an action, workflow, decision, control or incident; it may or may not be materially adverse.

Approval.definition: A bounded authorization decision that permits, conditions, rejects or stops a defined action or change.

Budget.definition: A bounded resource, value, iteration, time or transaction allowance used to constrain execution.

Control.definition: A governed objective and mechanism intended to prevent, constrain, detect, contain, recover from or provide assurance over a material condition or path.

Source.definition: An originating system, record set, repository, human-provided source or external source from which data or evidence is obtained.

EvidenceItem.definition: A versioned source object that supports, disputes, qualifies or bounds an assertion within stated scope, time and conditions.

AUTHENTICATES_AS.meaning: States that an actor, agent, application or workload establishes a session or request using a particular identity.

DELEGATES_TO.meaning: States that a grantor transfers bounded authority to a delegate.
DELEGATES_TO.constraint: Delegation retains grantor, scope, conditions, duration, approval and revocation semantics.

CONNECTS_TO.meaning: Represents network or logical connectivity from source to target.
CONNECTS_TO.constraint: Does not imply authentication, authorization, invocation or exploitability.

INVOKES.meaning: States that a source calls a tool, API, workflow, model endpoint or capability.
INVOKES.constraint: Invocation is distinct from ability to invoke, successful completion and resulting consequence.

TRIGGERS_ACTION.meaning: States that an entity or event directly causes a defined technical or business action.
TRIGGERS_ACTION.constraint: Must distinguish trigger from authority, successful effect and consequence.

AFFECTS.meaning: Links a threat, incident, action, finding or decision to a stakeholder, asset, process or outcome materially affected.
AFFECTS.constraint: Effect direction and scope must be stated.

APPROVED_BY.meaning: Links an action, relationship, use case, change or decision to its accountable approval.
APPROVED_BY.constraint: Approval must be meaningful, in scope and evidenced.

LIMITED_BY.meaning: Links authority, action or resource consumption to a constraint such as value, rate, time, scope, iteration or budget limit.
LIMITED_BY.constraint: Limit existence does not prove enforcement.

CONTROLLED_BY.meaning: States that an object, action, data flow or behavior is governed or constrained by a control.
CONTROLLED_BY.constraint: Directional counterpart of control coverage; effectiveness still requires evidence.

OBSERVED_BY.meaning: States that an object, relationship or event is directly or indirectly observed by an evidence source.
OBSERVED_BY.constraint: Observation does not imply approval or truth beyond source limitations.

EVIDENCED_BY.meaning: Links an object, relationship, path, control result or finding to one or more evidence items.
EVIDENCED_BY.constraint: Evidence strength is evaluated separately through grade, quality and confidence.

nodes.label: Analyst
nodes.summary: The human analyst who starts the refund workflow.

nodes.label: Analyst identity
nodes.summary: The identity the analyst signs in with. It is the grantor that delegates bounded authority to the agent.

nodes.label: Refund agent
nodes.summary: An AI agent that prepares and submits customer refunds on the analyst's behalf.

nodes.label: Refund tool
nodes.summary: A write-capable tool the agent calls to submit a refund.

nodes.label: Issue refund
nodes.summary: The business action that moves money. Its consequence is what makes this path material.

nodes.label: Customer refunded
nodes.summary: The intended result of the action. Whether it is materially adverse depends on the amount, the recipient and the conditions.

nodes.label: Payment ledger
nodes.summary: The system of record in which each refund appears. It is a source of evidence, not evidence of approval.

nodes.label: Refund limit
nodes.summary: A per-refund value allowance that constrains the action.

nodes.label: Refund approval
nodes.summary: The decision that permits, conditions or stops refunds above the limit.

nodes.label: Payment control
nodes.summary: A control intended to prevent or detect improper refunds. Coverage alone does not establish operating effectiveness.

nodes.label: Approval record
nodes.summary: The record of an approval decision. Its grade, quality and confidence are evaluated separately.

nodes.label: Control test record
nodes.summary: The record of a test of the payment control. Its grade, quality and confidence are evaluated separately.

relationships.conditions: The analyst's session is established with the analyst identity.
The scope, duration and revocation of this delegation have not been evidenced, so the step stays UNKNOWN.
The agent can reach the tool endpoint. Reaching it is a separate fact from being allowed to call it.
The agent calls the tool. A call is a separate fact from a successful refund.
A successful call issues the refund.
The refund pays the customer. Direction and scope: one customer, one refund.
Each refund is recorded in the payment ledger.
Each refund is capped at a set value. Whether the cap is enforced is a separate question.
Refunds above the limit need this approval.
The refund falls within the payment control's coverage.
The approval decision is linked to its record.
The control is linked to the record of its latest test.
